definition.interpretation: The observed divergence ratio of 0.229 falls well below the predicted threshold of 1.2, indicating that the tested perturbation frequency and coupling model do not drive the anticipated trajectory divergence within this specific parameter space.
definition.limitations: The experiment relied on a simplified random-seed perturbation model which may lack the state-space complexity required for authentic divergent intelligence modeling.
definition.next_step: Revise the hypothesis to account for lower baseline divergence and investigate whether coupling density or internal state persistence (memory) creates more robust divergence than external perturbation alone.

assumptions: State divergence can be measured via trajectory variance.
Internal state transitions in the target system are path-dependent.
definition.falsification: If increasing internal state memory depth does not yield significantly higher trajectory divergence than increasing external perturbation, the hypothesis that internal state drives divergence is falsified.
definition.statement: Trajectory divergence in intelligent systems is more sensitive to internal state-dependence (memory persistence) than external perturbation frequency; where external volatility fails to produce divergence, path-dependent internal state updates are the dominant differentiator.
definition.uncertainty: The magnitude of internal memory contribution relative to environmental noise remains unquantified.
